title: Count the Number of Good Nodes
summary: Given a tree with nodes numbered from 0 to n-1, count how many nodes have children subtrees of equal size.
statement: Given a tree with nodes numbered from 0 to n-1, count how many nodes have children subtrees of equal size. The tree is defined by edges connecting nodes, and a node is considered good if all its direct children have subtrees of the same size.
constraints: edges describes an undirected tree rooted at node 0 with 2≤n≤100,000.
A node is good when all subtrees rooted at its direct children have equal size.
Leaves and nodes with one child are good; return the total good-node count.
hints: Whether a node is good depends on child subtree sizes, which are known after its descendants.
Root the tree iteratively, then process the discovery order backward.
Store parent and subtree size; compare the set of direct-child sizes and accumulate each size into its parent.
Reverse order is postorder, so every compared child size is complete; the set condition exactly states equality.
editorial: Reverse order is postorder, so every compared child size is complete; the set condition exactly states equality.

tests.explanation: Every internal node has equal child-subtree sizes and all leaves are good, totaling seven.
Six nodes meet the equal-child-size condition.
